pull_request.title: prove: mm ktests with strengthened VmReader/VmWriter contracts
pull_request.body:
## Specs and properties supplemented by the ktest verification

### 1. New proof function in the specs layer (`ostd/specs/mm/io.rs`)

| Addition | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `VmIoOwner::tracked_shrink_range_front(nbytes)` | Shrinks the owner's range to its front `nbytes` bytes, preserving `id` / `is_kernel` / `is_fallible` / `mem_view` plus the three view-predicate implications — so the caller's `wf` relation survives a `limit` of the window (both limit tests rely on it) |

### 2. Contract additions in `mm::io` (`ostd/src/mm/io.rs`)

| API | Properties added |
|---|---|
| `VmWriter::from` / `VmReader::from` (reshaped from the `From` trait during the migration) | Full owner out-param contracts: `inv`, `wf(owner)`, view kind (write_view / read_view_initialized), `cursor.range == owner.range`, `owner.range.len == slice.len()`, kernel bounds (gated with `len == 0 \|\|` for the empty-slice case) |
| Infallible `write_val` | `avail >= size_of::<T>() ==> r is Ok` (kernel-space writes cannot fault); `avail < size_of::<T>() ==> r == Err(InvalidArgs)`; `final(owner).has_write_view()` (unconditional); the Err branch pins both `*self` and `*owner` |
| Infallible `read_val` | Same family: bidirectional Ok/Err conditions, `final(owner).read_view_initialized()`, Err branch pins both `*self` and `*owner` |
| Infallible `read_once` | Short-read `==> Err(InvalidArgs)` row plus Err-branch double pinning |
| Fallible `write_val` / `read_val` | Sufficient condition for the shortfall direction: `==> r == Err(InvalidArgs)` |
| `has_remain` / `has_avail` | `returns remain_spec() > 0` / `avail_spec() > 0` (exact boolean) |
| `limit` (reader and writer) | Exact value `== (if old <= max { old } else { max })` |
| `to_fallible` (reader and writer) | Symmetric `requires self.inv()` / `ensures r.inv()` |

### 3. Rustdoc / contract alignment

`read_val`'s Verified Properties section now states what the contract actually
delivers instead of promising a nonexistent `val_owner` — the documented root
cause of why the original value assertions could not be restored.
pull_request.bodyHTML:
Specs and properties supplemented by the ktest verification

1. New proof function in the specs layer (ostd/specs/mm/io.rs)

Addition Purpose
VmIoOwner::tracked_shrink_range_front(nbytes) Shrinks the owner's range to its front nbytes bytes, preserving id / is_kernel / is_fallible / mem_view plus the three view-predicate implications — so the caller's wf relation survives a limit of the window (both limit tests rely on it)

2. Contract additions in mm::io (ostd/src/mm/io.rs)

API Properties added
VmWriter::from / VmReader::from (reshaped from the From trait during the migration) Full owner out-param contracts: inv, wf(owner), view kind (write_view / read_view_initialized), cursor.range == owner.range, owner.range.len == slice.len(), kernel bounds (gated with len == 0 || for the empty-slice case)
Infallible write_val avail >= size_of::<T>() ==> r is Ok (kernel-space writes cannot fault); avail < size_of::<T>() ==> r == Err(InvalidArgs); final(owner).has_write_view() (unconditional); the Err branch pins both *self and *owner
Infallible read_val Same family: bidirectional Ok/Err conditions, final(owner).read_view_initialized(), Err branch pins both *self and *owner
Infallible read_once Short-read ==> Err(InvalidArgs) row plus Err-branch double pinning
Fallible write_val / read_val Sufficient condition for the shortfall direction: ==> r == Err(InvalidArgs)
has_remain / has_avail returns remain_spec() > 0 / avail_spec() > 0 (exact boolean)
limit (reader and writer) Exact value == (if old <= max { old } else { max })
to_fallible (reader and writer) Symmetric requires self.inv() / ensures r.inv()

3. Rustdoc / contract alignment

read_val's Verified Properties section now states what the contract actually
delivers instead of promising a nonexistent val_owner — the documented root
cause of why the original value assertions could not be restored.

**Type:** api-postconditions
**Problem:** This unconditional `KERNEL_BASE_VADDR <= r.cursor.vaddr` is false for an empty slice (the Rust pointer may dangle at a low address) even though `from` requires nothing beyond the slice; the sibling `from_kernel_space` contracts gate both bounds with `len == 0 ||` (ostd/src/mm/io.rs:251-252, 707-708), and the `VmReader::from` twin at :2053 has the same issue. Gate both rows with `old(slice).len() == 0 ||` — strictly weaker, so the existing body still discharges it.

review_comments.body:
**Type:** api-postconditions
**Problem:** The doc above this contract promises that "the returned `val_owner` owns the bytes backing `val`", but the `ensures` never binds a `val_owner` and constrains nothing about `val`'s contents — under the current model (`axiom_kernel_mem_view` yields arbitrary initialized bytes) such facts are underivable, which is why value assertions were dropped from the migrated tests. Either qualify the doc sentence to what callers actually get, or extend the contract with a val-owner out-param before restoring value assertions in tests.

review_comments.body:
**Type:** complete-external-contracts
**Problem:** `limit` mutates `end` but takes no tracked owner, so the caller's `wf(owner)` tie is silently broken and every caller must remember to shrink the owner with the same window via `tracked_shrink_range_front` (as ostd/src/mm/test.rs:272-277, :317-321 now do). Consider an owner-taking `limit_in_place` mirroring `skip_in_place` (ostd/src/mm/io.rs:1690s) whose ensures re-establish `wf`, so call sites cannot desynchronize the two numbers.

review_comments.body:
**Type:** api-postconditions
**Problem:** The Err branch of the added `match r` pins only `*old(self) == *final(self)` — the owner gets no `*old(owner) == *final(owner)` on error even though the early-return body never touches it; the same gap recurs in `read_val` and `read_once`. Add the owner equality to each Err arm so callers can rely on no-owner-drift on error.

review_comments.body:
**Type:** reuse-existing-specifications, upstream-reusable-specs
**Problem:** Vendored vstd already publishes both facts — `size_of::<u8>() == 1` in `layout_of_primitives` and `align_of_u8` (tools/verus/source/vstd/layout.rs:157, :268), consumed directly at ostd/src/cpu/set.rs:75 — so this pin is a second trust source; the recorded counterpoints are that the pin is codegen-checked (vstd's row is an unchecked axiom) and vstd excludes `align_of_u8` from default broadcasts over time-out. Either consume the vstd facts in `lemma_primitive_layout` and drop the pin, or record the rationale in-file — and either way keep an upstream proposal note for the u8 row.
